question: 10:39 Alert: rejects on voice-verification after config push.
reference:
Root cause: A typo passed review because the config had no schema bounds. The push went to all hosts at once.
Remediation: Validate config against bounds in CI and roll config out in stages, with automatic rollback on error rate.

question: 04:19 Alert: CPU on gateway above 16 percent.
reference:
Root cause: The minimum replica count was set for last year's traffic and scale-up was slower than the morning ramp.
Remediation: Review minimum replicas against current peak each quarter, and pre-scale ahead of the known daily ramp.

question: 22:42 Handshake failure alarm for notifications.
reference:
Root cause: The new library default raised the minimum protocol version and nobody knew which clients used old versions.
Remediation: Measure client protocol versions before changing defaults and give a published deprecation window.

question: 01:46 Blocked queries on billing triggered the page.
reference:
Root cause: Adding a column with a default rewrote the entire table while holding an exclusive lock.
Remediation: Migrate online: nullable column first, batched backfill, default last. Rehearse on production-sized data.

question: 06:55 Oldest-message age on billing passed 67 minutes.
reference:
Root cause: A malformed message crashed the consumer on each retry. No dead-letter path existed.
Remediation: Create a dead-letter queue with a retry cap and alert on oldest message age as well as depth.

question: 04:05 Alert: rising 401s on scheduler.
reference:
Root cause: The time daemon on scheduler-3de lost its upstream source and the node free-ran. Token validity windows are shorter than the drift.
Remediation: Alert on clock offset above 1 second. Run at least three time sources. Evict nodes with bad offset automatically.

question: 08:54 On-call paged for slow responses from auth-240.
reference:
Root cause: Peers were missing the intermediate authority that signed the new certificate, and nothing in the rotation tooling tested trust before cutover.
Remediation: Test the new certificate with real peers before cutover, and push the intermediate into trust stores ahead of any rotation.

question: 12:27 Latency alarm on one shard of auth, served from auth-43e.
reference:
Root cause: Shard choice depended on the customer id only, so one huge customer overloaded a shard.
Remediation: Salt hot keys, watch per-shard load, and limit request rate per key.

question: 06:32 Alert: outbound request rate from voice-verification 45x normal.
reference:
Root cause: Retry logic had no backoff and no retry budget, so each failure produced more load.
Remediation: Use exponential backoff with jitter, cap retries per request and per client, and honor Retry-After.

question: 06:11 Alert: 503s from billing, error rate above 16 percent.
reference:
Root cause: A new query path held connections during a slow downstream call. Pool size was never sized for that hold time.
Remediation: Release connections before downstream calls, add a pool-wait timeout alert, and size the pool from measured hold time.

question: 22:14 Errors toward a single upstream were flagged for voice-verification.
reference:
Root cause: A 24 hour TTL combined with a client library that cached lookups past the TTL.
Remediation: Reduce TTL ahead of DNS moves, make clients honor it, and drain a backend before it is retired.

question: 22:29 On-call got write-error alerts for scheduler-d71.
reference:
Root cause: A debug logging flag from a past investigation was never switched off, and rotation had no size limit.
Remediation: Set log size and retention limits, alert at 80 percent usage, and make debug flags expire on their own.

question: 16:32 Alert: CPU on gateway above 47 percent.
reference:
Root cause: The minimum replica count was set for last year's traffic and scale-up was slower than the morning ramp.
Remediation: Review minimum replicas against current peak each quarter, and pre-scale ahead of the known daily ramp.

question: 07:28 Dependency calls from notifications returned 401.
reference:
Root cause: A 90 day credential had no owner for its renewal.
Remediation: Rotate credentials automatically, alert two weeks before expiry, and assign an owner to each credential.

question: 17:19 Reject rate on scheduler jumped right after the config push.
reference:
Root cause: A one-digit typo went through review since nothing enforced allowed ranges, and the change hit every host together.
Remediation: Enforce value ranges in CI and ship config in stages, rolling back on error-rate alarms.

question: 00:03 Alert: database load behind search at its limit.
reference:
Root cause: All keys were written with the same TTL during a bulk refresh, so they expired in the same second.
Remediation: Add random jitter to TTLs, coalesce concurrent misses for the same key, and warm the cache before bulk expiry.

question: 21:01 Alert: 503s from scheduler, error rate above 67 percent.
reference:

Remediation: Release connections before downstream calls, add a pool-wait timeout alert, and size the pool from measured hold time.

reference:

question: 05:09 Pager noted scheduler-cd8 restarting every few hours.
reference:
Root cause: A cache added in 2.4.0 was keyed per request and had no eviction.
Remediation: Give each cache a size bound and eviction, and alarm on memory growth in canary hosts.

question: 10:00 Alert: 429 responses from auth.
reference:
Root cause: The reload read a config path that was empty during deployment and silently fell back to defaults.
Remediation: Fail the reload when the config is empty, and alert when active limits differ from the intended values.

question: 19:50 Alert: 401s from dependency on gateway.
reference:
Root cause: The credential had a 90 day life and nobody owned the rotation reminder.
Remediation: Automate credential rotation, alert 14 days before expiry, and name an owner for every credential.

question: 12:17 Latency alarm on one shard of search, served from search-8a5.
reference:
Root cause: Shard choice depended on the customer id only, so one huge customer overloaded a shard.
Remediation: Salt hot keys, watch per-shard load, and limit request rate per key.

question: 17:57 Many leadership changes were reported for scheduler.
reference:
Root cause: Lease timeout was shorter than the longest garbage collection pause seen on scheduler-9a6.
Remediation: Make lease timeouts longer than worst-case pauses and alert on more than two leader changes per hour.

question: 09:24 Alert: queries on auth blocked.
reference:
Root cause: The migration added a column with a default and rewrote the whole table under an exclusive lock.
Remediation: Use online migration patterns: add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then set the default. Test migrations on production-sized data.

question: 21:27 CPU on gateway passed 36 percent.
reference:
Root cause: The replica floor reflected old traffic levels, and scaling was slower than the morning ramp.
Remediation: Check the replica floor against current peaks every quarter and scale ahead of the known morning ramp.

question: 17:09 Pager fired on a 24 percent error rate for billing.
reference:
Root cause: Connections were held open while waiting on a slow downstream service, and the pool had not been sized for that.
Remediation: Do not hold connections across downstream calls. Alert on pool wait time. Choose pool size from measured hold time.

question: 21:44 Outbound traffic from ledger hit 50 times its norm.
reference:
Root cause: Retries happened immediately with no budget, so failures created more traffic.
Remediation: Exponential backoff with jitter, a retry cap per request and per client, and respect for Retry-After.

question: 21:45 Pager noted notifications-e5f restarting every few hours.
reference:
Root cause: A cache added in 6.0.1 was keyed per request and had no eviction.
Remediation: Give each cache a size bound and eviction, and alarm on memory growth in canary hosts.

question: 13:21 Latency rose on search even though traffic was low.
reference:
Root cause: Batch and serving pods shared a node and the batch job had no CPU limit.
Remediation: Apply CPU limits and priority classes, and run batch jobs on a separate node pool.
